The effects of electron finite Larmor radius (FLR) effects on tearing mode instabilities are examined through a linearized two-fluid model. The analysis reveals that when electrons are treated with finite Larmor radius effects, a parity instability emerging on fine scales ($m_f \gg 1$) arises. This mode is consistently quelled by either elevated electron temperatures or substantial electron cyclotron frequency. Furthermore, for these high-order electron modes, determining their growth rate requires accounting for magnetic drifts, whereas these drifts play no role in determining the growth rate of low-order electron modes.

In contrast, high-order ion tearing modes, which also incorporate the electron FLR effects, remain odd parity. However, similar to the electron fine-scale case, both magnetic drifts and higher-order FLR impacts suppress the instability of both modes. Additionally, while including the electron FLR effects can induce a parity instability for high-order tearing modes, this instability is suppressed if the electron temperature is sufficiently high.

The study also identifies the specific magnetic shear conditions under which the fine-scale tearing mode exhibits a parity instability. The results indicate that when magnetic shear is positive, this mode exhibits odd parity, whereas it exhibits even parity under conditions of negative magnetic shear.

The challenge of fashion instance-level image retrieval (FIR) is vital for real-world applications, yet it remains difficult due to extensive fashion instance overlap within complex backgrounds and sparse text labels. To tackle these hurdles, we introduce **ReRankNet**, a method for re-ranking candidate images using a contrastive learning framework optimized for FIR. ReRankNet employs a novel multi-scale training strategy that trains the network by pulling candidate images closer to a reference image in every scale during execution. Specifically, it optimizes multi-scale image representations through a specialized objective that enforces stricter constraints on lower-scale representations, thereby enhancing the discriminative ability of high-scale representations against similar visual patterns. Comprehensive experiments across two datasets—FashionIQ and COCO—under FIR settings demonstrate that ReRankNet significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches.

This article introduces an explicit semidiscrete $L^2$ gradient flow scheme designed for solving the gradient flow derived from general convex, lower semicontinuous functionals defined in $L^2$. These methods address ill-posed problems characterized by infinite-dimensional domains, requiring infinite-dimensional inputs, and often lack sufficiently smooth initial exact solutions. We demonstrate that truncating these semidiscrete numerical approximations at a strategically chosen time yields convergent regularized approximations. We then evaluate the impacts of both temporal truncation and initial data smoothing on the error bounds for approximate solutions. Furthermore, we establish error estimates applicable when the error in the test function remains bounded below away from zero. Our findings encompass rigorous results for three widely recognized regularization techniques: Tikhonov regularization, continuous stopping time methods, and the continuous analogue of Landweber iteration.

In this work, we introduce a new cost construction method for depth estimation that builds upon recent progress in view synthesis and 3D reconstruction techniques. Additionally, to ensure cost consistency with the synthesized views, we implement a novel consistency loss function. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that our method achieves superior depth estimation accuracy even in scenarios featuring occlusions and dynamic changes when used alongside current top-tier metrics.

This paper introduces a channel load aware (CLOA) mechanism for mobile home environments, replacing standard RSSI-based association with an RSSI and channel load integrated approach. The goal is to boost throughput and minimize delay. The author proposes a lightweight channel load measurement technique that effectively captures real-time data while reducing computational overhead. The proposed CLOA algorithm dynamically selects the optimal access point (AP) and channel by combining measured channel load with signal strength. Simulation results demonstrate that the CLOA algorithm outperforms traditional RSSI-based methods, achieving up to 13.6% higher average throughput and 10.6% lower delay. Furthermore, the proposed channel load measurement method is computationally efficient, consuming only 0.0001 seconds per measurement.
